title: IDisposable and using
summary: Releasing files, connections and other resources on time - how the garbage collector works and what it does not do, IDisposable, using statements and declarations, try/finally underneath, implementing Dispose in your own classes, IAsyncDisposable, and scoped helpers built on using.

cards.q: Why is the garbage collector not enough for files?
cards.a:
It frees memory at some unknown later time, but a file must be closed promptly

The collector runs when memory is needed, which may be much later. A file must be closed promptly so its data is written and other programs can open it.

cards.q: What does a using statement guarantee?
cards.a:
Dispose is called when the block is left, normally or by an exception

`using` works like try/finally around the block: `Dispose` always runs. It does not catch the exception, which still reaches the caller.

cards.q: A class has a private StreamWriter field. What should the class do?
cards.a:
Implement IDisposable and dispose the writer in its own Dispose method

An owner of a disposable resource must be disposable itself and release what it owns.
